title: La Leyenda Pirata — Gauntlet Loop
goal: Mobile Three.js pirate game (island builder + open-sea sailing + raids) built from the CC0 Pirate Nation voxel assets.
bar: Art direction: official Pirate Nation media (the shipped game built from these exact assets). UI objects and retention: Clash of Clans / Clash Royale. HUD layout and restraint: Kingshot. Our screenshots must win a blind side-by-side against them.

pieces.name: Asset pipeline
pieces.bar: Every model loads at a sane size with its animation clips intact, under 300KB.

rounds.summary: 36 models fetched from the CC0 library and optimized to .glb (9.5MB total, animations preserved). Models rendered at wildly wrong scales.
rounds.gap: Model normalization is broken: three.js, the glTF node transforms, and the GPU disagree about how big a skinned model is — the foundry rendered ~200 units instead of 5.

rounds.summary: Root cause found and split in two: gltf-transform's flatten/join double-applied armature transforms on skinned models, and no analytical method measures these models correctly. Pipeline now skips flatten/join for skinned documents, and sizes are calibrated from rendered pixels.

Sizes calibrated by rendering each model's silhouette under an orthographic camera of known extent. Found the last cause of the scale bug: every clip re-asserts the armature's normalizing scale on frame one, so a model's size was only valid until the mixer ticked. The pipeline now drops root scale tracks; parts still animate as authored.
rounds.gap: Fourteen models remain over the 300KB budget. Voxel models carry tiny palette textures, so converting them to vertex colours should collapse those to one material each.

rounds.summary: Terrain, stepped beach/grass plateaus, sand paths and the voxel water shader render correctly. Buildings blocked on the scale bug.
rounds.gap: Water reads too dark and too uniformly blue; foam is evenly scattered where the reference clusters it near the shore. No buildings visible yet.

rounds.summary: Terrain rebuilt to the measured recipe: island scaled to 26 cells with taller steps, beach ring stepping up to a plateau, grass plots stamped as rounded rectangles with sand between them reading as paths, sun/shade wall colours baked into vertex colours, and lighting retuned to the reference's bright low-contrast exposure.
rounds.gap: The terrain still has no surface noise at all - the reference has 25 unique colours in a patch where we have 1 - and the plots are laid out arbitrarily rather than composed.

rounds.summary: With the chrome fixed, the verification found the gap had moved to the world: our HUD is now the better-looking half of our own screenshot. Measured, not asserted - sea luminance std-dev 10.7 against the reference's 26.9, detail pixels 10.1% against 24.9%, and empty grass plots reading as unpainted rectangles.
rounds.gap: The amount of water is right (40.2% of frame against the reference's 43.1%). The texture is not. A round is running with those numbers as its acceptance criteria.

rounds.summary: Ocean rewritten from measurements taken off the reference: flat surface, 12-step dithered depth ramp keyed to a true shoreline distance field, view ramp fogging toward the horizon, near-camera darkening, clustered two-tier elongated foam decaying exponentially from the shore, and a solid waterline collar.
rounds.gap: Open-water foam is still denser than the reference's 0.7-1.5%, and the shallow shelf reads flatter than the measured 90-110px gradient.

pieces.name: HUD and panels (Clash objects, Kingshot layout)

rounds.summary: Clash UI language reverse-engineered into a 1600-line implementation spec (src/ui/UI_SPEC.md): full token palette, the four-layer rule that makes a surface read as Clash (constant-weight ink contour, hard gloss step at ~50%, warm top rim, dark lip with zero-offset extrusion), portrait and landscape layouts, and component specs.
rounds.gap: Nothing implemented yet - the spec exists, the HUD does not.

rounds.summary: HUD restructured to Kingshot's layout: four corner clusters became one bottom bar with five slots, seven separately-framed pills became one translucent capsule with dividers, building timers became dark capsules, and the sim's next-action verdict is now stated in words above the bar. Chrome hides 16.9% of the portrait screen; against Clash we win on chrome.
rounds.gap: The four-layer rule was being applied per component by hand, so each round fixed some objects and regenerated the defect in others. Now enforced by npm run audit:layers, which measures the rendered pixels.

pieces.name: Economy, save and daily hooks
pieces.bar: A session leaves a timer running and something to collect; reopening applies offline production. See RETENTION.md.

rounds.summary: Economy, persistence and the daily hooks built: balance.json holds every tuning number, src/sim/ is pure and deterministic, IndexedDB persistence with export/import, and 88 tests including the storage invariant at every town hall level and a greedy 24h playthrough that must never strand the player.
rounds.gap: Verified by finger in a real browser: a builder can be spent both ways and the retention rule holds for 0 minutes of violation. Missing: the tutorial director, so a new game ships the opening session's result rather than its performance.

rounds.summary: Retention design made concrete: beat-by-beat first three minutes (first tap before 10s, two buildings and two collections inside 32s, first real timer at 45s, first chest pre-aged so opening costs exactly 1 gem), plus full balance tables for producers, storages, town hall and chests.
rounds.gap: Corrections to RETENTION.md not yet folded in: start with 2 builders not 1, producer cap and storage cap are two different mechanics, and total storage must exceed the most expensive unlock by 25% or the player hits a hard wall.

rounds.summary: Build mode and the upgrade sheet shipped, so the builder - the scarce resource the whole loop hangs on - can finally be spent. Picker, ghost placement on the grid, confirm/cancel, and a sheet with a 2x2 stat grid and the cost on the CTA.
rounds.gap: Four economy defects found by verification and fixed: paying gems charged and did nothing, chest loot was destroyed while the reveal announced the roll, level 1 was free and instant for every copy, and the Lleno chip upgraded the wrong store.
